summary: Ran all four acceptance checks against the production build of the app: all four pass.
The /invoices table now reads INV-1005 → INV-1001, newest issue date first; the export button, the total and the CSV are untouched.
Also probed a reload, a client-side nav into the page, and three interleaved table/export requests — the new order never leaks into the CSV.

blocks.caption: Before (parent commit 73abefb, built and served separately): the table reads INV-1001 at the top down to INV-1005 — seeded order, oldest issue date first.

Acceptance check 1 — after: the same page now reads INV-1005, INV-1004, INV-1003, INV-1002, INV-1001 top to bottom, the exact reverse. Acceptance check 2 is in this same shot: the button still reads 'Export 3 invoices as CSV' and the line below still reads 'Total sent: $1,497.50'.
Acceptance check 2, read out of the served HTML rather than off the screenshot: the button label and the total both match the expected strings character for character.

blocks.caption: Acceptance check 3, exercised both ways: curl against /invoices/export, and clicking the export button in Chromium and opening the downloaded file. Both give the header row then INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003, with INV-1004 and INV-1005 absent — the table's new order does not reach the CSV.
Acceptance check 4: `npm test` — 32 tests across 4 files, all passing. The parent commit ran 28, so this change adds 4 and breaks none of the existing ones.

Acceptance check 4, the two cases the check names specifically: the tie case ('issued on the same day … in the order they were given') and the non-mutation case ('leaves the list it was given in its original order') both exist and both pass, alongside the page-level row-order test.

Ways this could look right but be wrong, each tried on the running app: a reload, clicking in from /, interleaved table-then-export requests checking the sort does not leak, a second export click, the one console error (a pre-existing favicon 404), and whether the order tracks issuedOn or the id.

focus.title: The sort copies the shared list, and that matters here
focus.detail: listInvoices() hands the same readonly array to both the page and the export route. newestFirst() spreads before sorting, so the export still sees seeded order. I checked this at runtime rather than trusting the unit test: loading /invoices and then fetching /invoices/export, three times alternating, returned INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003 every time.

focus.title: The new order is visible only as row order
focus.detail: The table shows Invoice, Customer, Amount, Status — there is no issue-date column, which the spec puts out of scope. So nothing on screen explains why the rows sit in that order. I cross-checked the displayed order against the seeded issuedOn values (INV-1005 is 2026-11-08, INV-1001 is 2026-10-02) to confirm it is genuinely date order and not just reversed-by-id, which would look identical on this data.

focus.title: The CSV and the table now disagree on order, on purpose
focus.detail: The table reads newest first; the CSV still reads INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003. The spec calls this out as deliberate and leaves app/invoices/export/route.ts untouched. It is correct against the spec as written, but it is the thing a reader is most likely to file as a bug later, so it is worth a decision rather than a shrug.
